700140.t: Cognate with Mycenaean Greek 𐀀𐀐𐀫 (a-ke-ro), with further origin uncertain.

700159.t: From Proto-Hellenic *hágiyos, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁yáǵ-yo-s, from *h₁yaǵ- (“to sacrifice, worship”).

700120.t: A Proto-Indo-European etymology as a compound *m̥ǵh₂-peh₂- (from *méǵh₂- (“great”) + *peh₂- (“to protect”), literally “[provide] great protection”) was proposed by Pinault in 1991; see ἀγα- (ăgă-, “way too”) for the first component.

700106.t: Possibly from Proto-Hellenic *əgatʰós, from Proto-Indo-European *m̥ǵh₂dʰh₁ós (“made great; whose deeds are great”), from *méǵh₂s (“great”) + *dʰeh₁- (“do”) + *-ós. Compare Latin magnificus from same roots.

700196.t: From Proto-Hellenic *agrós, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂éǵros. Cognates include Mycenaean Greek 𐀀𐀒𐀫 (a-ko-ro), Latin ager, Sanskrit अज्र (ájra) and Old English æcer (English acre).

700191.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂éǵr̥yos (“campestral, of a field”). By surface analysis, ἀγρός (agrós, “field, country”) + -ιος (-ios, adjective suffix).

700175.t: From ἀ- (a-, “not”), the root of γιγνώσκω (gignṓskō, “know”) + -έω (-éō, verb-forming suffix). Compare ἀγνώς (agnṓs, “unknown”), ἄγνοια (ágnoia, “ignorance”).

700177.t: From ἀ- (a-, “not”) + γιγνώσκω (gignṓskō, “know”) + -ια (-iā, abstract noun suffix).

700178.t: From Proto-Hellenic *hagnós, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁yáǵ-nós, from *h₁yaǵ- (“to sacrifice; to worship”). Cognate with Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hyaȷ́nás.

700183.t: From Proto-Hellenic *agorā́, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂goréh₂, from *h₂ger- (“to gather”); equivalent to ἀγείρω (ăgeírō, “to gather”) + -α (-ā, abstract noun suffix). Cognate with Mycenaean Greek 𐀀𐀒𐀨 (a-ko-ra).

700179.t: From the adjective ἁγνός (hagnós, “chaste”), unless this is a folk etymology which led to the cultural associations with chastity, rather than the reverse.

700145.t: Traditionally derived from Proto-Indo-European *h₂éngos, from the root *h₂eng- (“to curve”), though Beekes prefers deriving the word from a Pre-Greek stratum, due to its semantic domain; many words for "vessel" are mentioned by Homer but are loaned from…

700113.t: From ἀγαλλιάω (agalliáō), form of ἀγάλλω (agállō, “to rejoice”) + -σις (-sis).

700119.t: From a root *ἀγαν- (*agan-) of uncertain origin plus a suffix -ακτέω (-aktéō, expressive formation suffix), as seen also in ὑλακτέω (hŭlaktéō, “to bark”).

700162.t: From a suffixed derivative of Proto-Indo-European *h₂enk- (“to curve, bend”), whence also ἄγκος (ánkos, “bend”), ἀγκύλος (ankúlos, “curved, bent”).

700172.t: From ἁγνός (hagnós, “sacred, pure”) + -ίζω (-ízō, denominative verb suffix).

700188.t: From ἀγρεύς (ăgreús, “hunter”) + -εύω (-eúō, verb-forming suffix), from ἄγρα (ắgrā, “hunt”); doublet of ἀγρέω (ăgréō).

700198.t: From ἄγρυπνος (ágrupnos, “sleepless, wakeful”) + -ία (-ĭ́ā, abstract noun suffix).

700116.t: From ἀγάλλομαι (agállomai, “to be proud, exult in”) + -μα (-ma).

700195.t: From ἀγρός (ăgrós) + οἰκέω (oikéō). For the opposition with ἀστεῖος (ăsteîos), compare typologically Latin agrestis (cognate via Proto-Indo-European *h₂éǵros), pāgānus, rūsticus vs. cīvīlis, urbānus.

700118.t: From Proto-Indo-European *m̥ǵ-éh₂-m, accusative singular of *méǵh₂s (“great”, whence μέγας (mégăs)).

700166.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂enk- (“corner, hirn”), the same source as ἄγκος (ắnkos, “glen; dell”), ἄγκυρα (ắnkūră, “anchor”) and ἀγκύλος (ănkŭ́los, “curved; bent”).
